claim: Proteomic analysis on Drosophila exposed to repeated TBI identified alterations in several novel molecular pathways.
source: We performed proteomic analysis on Drosophila exposed to repeated TBI and identified resultant alterations in several novel molecular pathways.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry analysis of Drosophila brains exposed to TBI, as described in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: TBI upregulated nuclear pore complex (NPC) proteins in Drosophila.
source: TBI upregulated nuclear pore complex (NPC) and nucleocytoplasmic transport (NCT) proteins as well as alter nucleoporin stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data showing upregulation of NPC proteins (Figure 1D, E) and qRT-PCR validation (Figure 1F-L).

claim: TBI upregulated nucleocytoplasmic transport (NCT) proteins in Drosophila.
source: TBI upregulated nuclear pore complex (NPC) and nucleocytoplasmic transport (NCT) proteins as well as alter nucleoporin stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data showing upregulation of NCT proteins (Figure 1D, E) and qRT-PCR validation (Figure 1M).

claim: Traumatic injury altered nucleoporin stability in Drosophila.
source: TBI upregulated nuclear pore complex (NPC) and nucleocytoplasmic transport (NCT) proteins as well as alter nucleoporin stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data showing that Nup214 protein levels remain elevated over time in larval and adult brains (Figure 1P-S).

claim: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 distribution in Drosophila.
source: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 and NPC protein distribution in flies and a rat model and led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing aberrant RanGAP1 staining in TBI-exposed Drosophila brains (Figure 2E, F).

claim: Traumatic injury disrupted NPC protein distribution in Drosophila.
source: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 and NPC protein distribution in flies and a rat model and led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing abnormal Mab414 staining in TBI-exposed Drosophila brains (Figure 2A, B).

claim: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 distribution in a rat model.
source: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 and NPC protein distribution in flies and a rat model and led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data showing RanGAP1 pathology in rat hippocampal regions following TBI (Figure 2H, I).

claim: Traumatic injury disrupted NPC protein distribution in a rat model.
source: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 and NPC protein distribution in flies and a rat model and led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data showing Nup62 pathology in rat hippocampal regions following TBI (Figure 2J, K).

claim: Traumatic injury led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43 in Drosophila.
source: Traumatic injury disrupted RanGAP1 and NPC protein distribution in flies and a rat model and led to coaggregation of NPC components and TDP-43.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing perinuclear and cytoplasmic coaggregation of Tbph and Mab414 in TBI-exposed Drosophila brains (Figure 2C, D).

claim: Trauma-mediated NCT defects are rescued by nuclear export inhibitors in vivo.
source: In addition, trauma-mediated NCT defects and lethality are rescued by nuclear export inhibitors.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that KPT-350 treatment protects against trauma-mediated depletion of nuclear GFP signal (Figure 3F, G).

claim: Trauma-mediated lethality is rescued by nuclear export inhibitors in vivo.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins in vivo triggered TDP-43 cytoplasmic mislocalization.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins in vitro triggered TDP-43 cytoplasmic mislocalization.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins in vivo triggered TDP-43 aggregation.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins in vitro triggered TDP-43 aggregation.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins altered TDP-43 solubility in vivo.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins reduced motor function in Drosophila.

claim: Genetic upregulation of nucleoporins reduced lifespan in Drosophila.

claim: NUP62 pathology is present in postmortem brain tissues of patients with mild CTE.
source: We also found NUP62 pathology and elevated NUP62 concentrations in postmortem brain tissues of patients with mild or severe CTE as well as co-localization of NUP62 and TDP-43 in CTE.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data showing widespread and intense NUP62 immunoreactivity in mild CTE brain tissues (Figure 6B).

claim: NUP62 pathology is present in postmortem brain tissues of patients with severe CTE.

claim: NUP62 concentrations are elevated in postmortem brain tissues of patients with severe CTE.

claim: NUP62 co-localizes with TDP-43 in CTE.

claim: TBI leads to NCT defects, which potentially mediate the TDP-43 pathology in CTE.

claim: TBI is one of the most common causes of death and disability worldwide.

claim: TBI is linked with development of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

claim: Postmortem brain tissues from repeated trauma patients show TDP-43 pathology.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Blennow et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2017; Mckee et al., 2018; McKee et al., 2010; Tan et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2015; Wiesner et al., 2018).

claim: Animal models of TBI show TDP-43 pathology.

claim: TDP-43 pathology is present in ~97% of ALS cases.

evidence: The claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations to published literature.

claim: TDP-43 regulates RNA processing such as gene transcription, mRNA splicing, mRNA stability, and mRNA transport and localization.

claim: Cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregates are abnormally phosphorylated and ubiquitinated.
